transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Well, I'm here because I'm having a lot of trouble at work lately. I work at a meat processing plant, and... I just keep starting my tasks, like the sanitation steps, the batch logs, or the end-of-line paperwork, but I somehow always leave out the last parts. 

It's really becoming a problem. I mean, I know my job depends on finishing everything correctly, but I just can't seem to follow through and actually complete the whole thing.
Do you find that you're forgetting to do the last parts of your tasks or do you just lose interest or get distracted?

I think it's more about getting distracted or just losing focus. I'll start a shift trying really hard to stay locked in and do everything right. But after a while, all the cutting, weighing, and checking labels... it just sort of blurs together. Next thing I know, I realize I’ve been staring at the same tray or the same log sheet for a few minutes, and I'm not even taking in what I’m supposed to do next. It's like my brain just checks out.
Do you feel anxious or overwhelmed when you're at work?

Not really anxious, no. I don't feel nervous or anything like that while I'm there. And I wouldn't say I feel overwhelmed by the work itself, either, because I know how to do all the steps. It's just... I just can't keep my attention on it. It's not a stressed feeling, just kind of a blank one.
Do you have trouble focusing or completing tasks outside of work as well?

I don't really know, honestly. I haven't really noticed it being an issue outside of work. I mean, I live alone, so if I don't finish folding laundry right away or whatever, it doesn't really matter. Work is where it's actually causing problems for me.
Do you often feel restless or fidgety when you're not working?

No, not really. I don't feel restless or like I need to be moving around all the time. I can sit still just fine when I'm at home watching TV or something. It's really just the focus part that's the issue, not feeling fidgety.
Have you been feeling sad or down most of the time lately?

No, not really. I don't feel sad or depressed or anything like that. My mood is generally fine. I mean, I get frustrated that I can't keep my focus at work, but I wouldn't say I'm feeling down most of the time.
Have you been having trouble focusing at work for a short time or has this been an issue for a while?

It's been a while, honestly. This has been a serious problem since I switched into full-time meat processing, which was about... two years and four months ago, I think. It's just been a struggle ever since I started doing that full-time.
Do you often feel like you're constantly on the go or have a lot of extra energy when you're not at work?

No, I don't. It's kind of like what I was saying earlier about not feeling fidgety. I really don't have a bunch of extra energy, and I definitely don't feel like I'm constantly on the go. When I'm off the clock, I'm pretty normal in that regard... I just like to relax. So no, that's not something I experience.
Have you experienced any significant life events or changes around the time your focus problems at work started?
No, not really. Aside from switching to the full-time meat processing job, nothing else major happened around that time. It was just the job change, really.
Did you have trouble paying attention or finishing tasks when you were in school?

Yes, I did. My mom actually still has some of my old elementary school report cards, like from around fourth grade, I think. The teachers would always write that I was bright, but that I needed constant reminders to actually finish my classwork and turn in my homework. I remember I would understand the lessons fine, but I'd just... miss big chunks of the instructions unless the teacher was right there making sure I was paying attention. So yeah, it's been an issue for a long time.
Do you feel upset or emotionally bothered by your inability to focus at work?

Um, no, I wouldn't say I get upset or emotionally bothered by it. I mean, it's definitely frustrating when I fall behind or mess something up, but I don't really get... down about it, I guess. It's just more of a practical issue for me. I just want to figure out how to get my work done properly without so much hassle, you know? So no, it doesn't really take an emotional toll on me like that.
Do you think you might be putting off certain tasks at work because you don't like doing them?

Well, it's not exactly that I don't like doing them... it's more about the type of task. Like, the physical part of the job is fine, but I definitely put off the certification modules. And any of the long procedure reading, I just avoid it until the absolute last possible minute. Sitting there, trying to focus and actually absorb all those safety rules and regulations... it just takes so much out of me. It honestly feels almost physically exhausting to force myself to read through all that text.

Do you think you're having trouble focusing at work because you're trying to avoid doing certain tasks or is it more that you just can't seem to keep your attention on them regardless of what they are?

I think it's more that I just can't keep my attention on them, regardless of what it is. Like, I can start my shift trying really hard to stay focused and locked in on what I'm doing. But after a while, all the cutting and weighing and checking labels... it all just kind of blurs together. I'll suddenly realize I've been staring at the same tray of meat or the same log sheet for a few minutes, and I'm not even taking in what I'm supposed to be doing next. So it's not really about avoiding the work, my brain just sort of checks out on its own.
Do you ever feel emotionally drained or upset after realizing you've lost focus at work?

No, not really. Like I mentioned before, I don't really get upset or emotionally bothered by it. It's frustrating, sure, but I don't feel emotionally drained or down about it when I realize my mind wandered. It's just more of an annoyance because it slows me down.
Do you ever feel anxious or stressed when you're not at work?

No, not really. I don't really feel anxious or stressed when I'm off the clock. I mean, I might be physically tired from standing and working all day, but I wouldn't say I'm stressed out. Once I leave work, I just kind of go home and relax. I don't really have that kind of worry or anxiety following me around.
Do you have trouble focusing when you're doing things you enjoy?

I haven't really noticed that happening. When I'm doing something I actually want to do, like hanging out or watching a movie, I don't think I have the same problem. I guess I'm usually able to just pay attention to it without my mind wandering off.
Do you have trouble focusing when you're reading or doing quiet activities at home?
No, not really. I don't read much, to be honest, but if I'm just sitting quietly at home, I don't feel like I'm struggling to focus. It's really just when I'm at work that I notice it happening.
Do you have trouble focusing when you're learning something new outside of work?

Not really, no. I mean, I haven't tried to learn a whole lot of new things since I finished my degree, but... if it's something I actually want to learn on my own time, I don't think I have an issue with it. It really just seems to be a problem when I'm on the clock at work.
Do you think your focus problems would happen if you were working in a different job or a different setting?

I'm honestly not sure. I've only been out of school for a little while, so this is my first real job since getting my degree. I work in a meat processing plant right now, and it's pretty repetitive, so maybe that's part of it? But I really don't know if I'd be struggling like this if I were doing something else or working somewhere different. I just haven't had the chance to find out yet.
Do you think you would have the same focus problems if you were in a work setting that was less repetitive than your current job?

I'm not really sure. It's hard to say because, like I mentioned, I haven't had another job since I graduated to compare it to. Maybe if I was doing something that changed more day to day, it wouldn't be as bad. But I honestly don't know if the focus issues would just follow me there anyway.
